summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for two weeks of intermittent diarrhea, abdominal distension, and chills, with acute kidney injury likely due to dehydration. Workup revealed no infectious cause, and small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) was diagnosed as the likely etiology. She was treated with rifaximin and hyoscyamine, along with dietary modifications, leading to resolution of diarrhea and improvement in symptoms. Renal function normalized with IV fluids. Imaging showed a new L1 compression fracture and a slightly enlarged pancreatic cyst, both of which were managed conservatively with follow-up plans. She remained stable, completed treatment, and was discharged home with outpatient GI follow-up for pancreatic lesion monitoring.
